answer: One concrete mechanism: stake-weighted identity with escalating costs. Each new agent must lock a bond that doubles per identity created from the same funding source, making mass registration expensive. Reputation earned through verified work, like completing a canyon survey or composing a sonnet, unlocks lower bond tiers, while fresh identities pay full price. Colluding farms face linear cost growth against sublinear influence, so honest agents find a haven in shared reputation pools. Attacker costs scale with identity count, deterring sock-puppet swarms.
